Current research in microbial sciences 2026-12-01 Medium

Ultra-deep HiFi sequencing reveals rare structural-variant subpopulations in multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa from an LVAD-associated infection.

This study uses ultra-deep HiFi long-read sequencing to characterize a multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolate from a left ventricular assist device (LVAD)-associated infection, revealing rare structural-variant subpopulations within the population. The work highlights genomic heterogeneity that standard sequencing depth may miss, with implications for antibiotic and phage therapy resistance.

Cancer science 2026-11-16 Medium

MARiO: Predicting Cancer Variant Pathogenicity by Integrating In Silico Evaluation and Patient-Level Mutational Contexts.

MARiO is a machine-learning model that predicts the pathogenicity of missense cancer variants by combining variant-level in silico features with patient-level mutational context, addressing the limitation of existing tools that ignore clinical context. This integration aims to improve variant interpretation in comprehensive genomic profiling for precision oncology, particularly for variants lacking established consensus.

Chembiochem : a European journal of chemical biology 2026-11-12 Medium

Catalytic DNA for Precision Diagnostics: DNAzyme-Based Approaches to Single-Nucleotide Polymorphism Detection.

This review examines DNAzyme-based biosensors for detecting single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), the most common form of human genetic variation and key biomarkers for disease risk and precision medicine. The authors argue that these catalytic DNA sensors offer advantages over conventional genotyping methods by combining programmable sequence recognition with isothermal catalytic signal amplification, enabling sensitive SNP detection even in complex biological samples.

Genome research 2026-11-10 Medium

Ultrafast alignment-free detection of viral genome variation with bronko.

The authors present bronko, an alignment-free framework that detects viral genome variation directly from sequencing reads using locality-sensitive bucketing and k-mer counting, avoiding the computational cost of traditional alignment-based variant calling. This approach enables scaling to massive viral sequencing datasets where standard pipelines become prohibitive.

The Journal of infectious diseases 2026-11-10 Medium

O-acetylation mediates four distinct structural variants of the pneumococcal vaccine serotype 15A capsule polysaccharide.

This study re-examined the capsule polysaccharides of pneumococcal serogroup 15 and found that O-acetylation generates four distinct structural variants of the 15A capsule, not just the previously recognized 15A/15F pair. The work shows that conventional serological and molecular typing can miss O-acetylation differences, which matters because 15A is included in newer conjugate vaccines and variant capsules may affect vaccine coverage and immune recognition.

Leveraging artificial intelligence for livestock genetics and breeding.

This review examines how artificial intelligence tools are being applied to livestock genetics and breeding, noting that while animal breeding has long used data-driven prediction, modern AI approaches remain at an early stage with substantial untapped potential. The authors survey current applications and likely future directions for AI in improving milk, meat, and egg production.

Integrated optimization of experimental and computational workflows improves genome recovery in long-read gut metagenomics.

This study systematically evaluates and optimizes a long-read metagenomic workflow for gut microbiome samples, spanning sample processing through computational assembly, to improve recovery of complete microbial genomes. By integrating experimental and computational optimizations, the authors show that long-read approaches can overcome the fragmentation limits of short-read sequencing and yield more contiguous, complete genomes.

Proteomics-Guided Discovery of Candidate Enzymes for Degradation of a Rare Pyruvylated Glycosaminogalactan by a Newly Isolated Luteolibacter Strain.

The authors isolated a new Luteolibacter strain capable of degrading EPSLp, a rare pyruvylated glycosaminogalactan exopolysaccharide, and used proteomics to identify candidate CAZymes involved in its breakdown. This work expands knowledge of carbohydrate-active enzyme diversity by linking a previously uncharacterized EPS structure to specific bacterial enzymes.

Genome biology and evolution 2026-11-05 Medium

Conservative evolution of genetic and features in Caenorhabditis becei, an experimentally tractable gonochoristic worm.

The authors identify Caenorhabditis becei, a gonochoristic (male/female) nematode, as an experimentally tractable model for evolutionary genetics, addressing the field's heavy reliance on self-fertile hermaphroditic Elegans Group species. They show that transmission-genetic properties known from androdioecious Elegans Group species are conserved in this Japonica Group species, making it a useful new system for comparative genomics.

Molecular plant 2026-11-04 Medium

Large language and foundation models in predictive plant breeding: Capabilities, evidence, and challenges.

This review examines how large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, knowledge graphs, and biological foundation models can be applied to predictive plant breeding, covering knowledge mining, predictive modeling, and breeding design. The authors also conduct a systematic evidence audit, which appears to assess the strength of published evidence supporting these applications. The paper highlights both the promise and the current limitations of these AI tools in agricultural genomics.

Briefings in bioinformatics 2026-11-02 Medium

A recall-rescue fuzzy layer over paired Z-DNA Hunter scans for fast Z-DNA detection.

The authors present Z-DNA-Fuzzy Hunter 1.1.0, a tool that improves detection of Z-DNA-forming regions by combining a permissive scan (high recall) with a stringent scan (high precision) and integrating the results through a fuzzy expert layer. This dual-scan strategy addresses the sensitivity-specificity trade-off in sequence-based Z-DNA prediction, aiming to capture more true candidates while retaining high-confidence support. The method is fast and interpretable, extending the existing Z-DNA Hunter tool.

Briefings in bioinformatics 2026-11-02 Medium

Inferring causal networks for genomic trios with high-dimensional confounding variables.

The paper introduces a new method for inferring causal relationships between molecular phenotypes (like gene expression) using genetic variants as instruments under the Mendelian randomization principle, specifically designed to handle high-dimensional confounding variables such as other genes, processes, and demographic factors. Existing methods struggle with such high-dimensional confounders, so this work extends causal network inference to more realistic genomic trio settings.

Microbial genomics 2026-11-01 Medium

SCCmecExtractor: a tool for extracting staphylococcal cassette chromosome elements from whole-genome sequences.

SCCmecExtractor is a lightweight Python toolkit that identifies and extracts complete staphylococcal cassette chromosome (SCC) elements from whole-genome assemblies by detecting degenerate attachment site (att) patterns. Unlike existing SCCmec typing tools, it can extract the full element sequence and classify SCC elements that lack methicillin resistance genes, filling a gap in mobile genetic element analysis for staphylococci.

Environmental microbiology 2026-11-01 Medium

The Promise and Limitations of Metabolic Trait Prediction Across Diverse Bacteria.

This study tests the common assumption that bacterial metabolic traits can be reliably predicted from genome sequences alone. Comparing four popular bioinformatic tools against high-throughput growth phenotypes of 186 marine bacteria, the authors find that predictions for simple substrates are limited in accuracy and highly variable across taxa and substrates, with many strains incorrectly predicted. The work highlights important limitations of genome-based metabolic inference and cautions against over-reliance on such tools.

JID innovations : skin science from molecules to population health 2026-11-01 Medium

Long-read sequencing of FLG identifies extensive copy number variation in exon 3 and detects rare loss-of-function variants.

Using long-read sequencing on 192 samples from Belgium, Ireland, and Rwanda, the authors characterized the repetitive exon 3 of FLG, revealing extensive copy number variation and detecting both common and rare loss-of-function variants associated with atopic dermatitis. This approach overcomes the limitations of short-read sequencing in this repetitive region, improving variant detection for a key skin-barrier gene.

bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology 2026-10-31 Medium

Kidzoi Enables Cell-Type-Specific Regulatory Activity and Variant Effect Prediction in Kidney.

Kidzoi is a kidney cell-type-specific sequence-to-function deep learning model created by transfer learning from the pretrained Borzoi model using single-nucleus chromatin accessibility data. It enables prediction of regulatory activity and variant effects in a kidney-specific context, addressing the limitation that existing models are constrained by their original training datasets and cannot cover all cell types and conditions. This provides a practical route to specialize general S2F models for specific tissues without training de novo.

Integration of single-cell and bulk transcriptomics for deciphering prognostic value and immunotherapeutic features of floatptosis-mediated cell death in lung adenocarcinoma.

The authors built a prognostic model for lung adenocarcinoma based on genes related to floatptosis, a newly described vacuolar cell death pathway triggered by outer membrane vesicles from a Bergeyella cardium variant. They combined single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data to link these genes to patient survival and immunotherapy-related features. The work is exploratory and the clinical utility of the model remains to be validated.

Multi-omics and pathological landscape of a senescence-associated prognostic model in bladder urothelial carcinoma.

The authors built a senescence-associated prognostic model for bladder urothelial carcinoma by screening pan-cancer senescence signals and integrating multi-omics and pathological data. The model stratifies patients by risk and links senescence signatures to tumor microenvironment features, aiming to connect molecular characterization with potential clinical translation.

PoolParty: streamlined design of DNA sequence libraries in Python.

PoolParty is a new Python package that streamlines the design of DNA sequence libraries for massively parallel reporter assays, deep mutational scanning, and other multiplexed variant-effect experiments. It addresses the lack of purpose-built software that has made library design tedious and error-prone, and can also be used in silico to analyze genomic AI models.

Microbiology Galaxy Lab: a community-driven gateway for reproducible and FAIR analysis of microbiological data.

The authors present the Microbiology Galaxy Lab (MGL), a free, community-supported web platform built on Galaxy that gives microbiologists access to over 315 tool suites and 115 curated workflows for metabarcoding, (meta)genomic, and (meta)transcriptomic analyses. The platform aims to lower computational barriers and promote reproducible, FAIR analysis of the rapidly growing volume of microbial omics data.

Genomics & informatics 2026-10-28 Medium

Experimental benchmarking of in silico annotations at prostate cancer risk loci and hypothesis-generating cross-cancer prioritisation of ovarian risk variants.

The authors re-analyzed a massively parallel reporter assay (DiR-seq) testing 208 prostate cancer risk SNPs across three cell lines, identifying 50 regulatory SNPs under FDR control. They then benchmarked standard in silico annotation tools against these experimental results and used the findings to prioritize ovarian cancer risk variants by cross-cancer comparison. The work provides an experimentally grounded benchmark for computational regulatory variant annotation and a hypothesis-generating framework for linking non-coding risk variants to function.

Agent_K: An Agent-Orchestrated Pipeline for Mapping Genes to Biosynthetic Pathway towards Metabolite Discovery.

Agent_K is an agent-orchestrated framework that automates the entire workflow from bacterial whole-genome sequence analysis to biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) identification, pathway mapping, and candidate metabolite discovery. It addresses the fragmentation of existing computational tools by integrating data processing, annotation, and analysis across heterogeneous platforms with minimal manual intervention. This enables more streamlined genome-guided natural product discovery.

bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology 2026-10-23 High

Reference-free isoform discovery links unannotated RNA processing to disease risk.

The authors present Torino, a computational framework that discovers RNA processing patterns directly from population-scale RNA sequencing data without relying on existing transcript annotations. By adapting non-negative matrix factorization to model coverage variation across samples, Torino identifies unannotated RNA processing events and links them to disease risk across diverse tissues and disease states. This reference-free approach reveals disease-relevant isoform changes that are missed by annotation-dependent methods.

Streamline CNV - A Handy Nextflow Pipeline for Chromosomal Copy Number Variation Analysis.

Streamline CNV (SLCNV) is a new Nextflow-based pipeline that makes low-pass whole-genome sequencing copy number variation analysis accessible to wet-lab biologists without computational expertise. It provides a user-friendly, flexible workflow covering multiple copy number-related analyses, addressing the gap left by existing tools that require specialized bioinformatics skills.

Frontiers in microbiology 2026-01-01 Medium

cgMLST typing reproducibility is maintained across diverse whole-genome sequencing workflows in a multi-country HERA2 surveillance pilot.

Six European public health labs sequenced the same 25 bacterial isolates using their own routine WGS workflows, then compared cgMLST-based typing results. Despite differences in laboratory methods, cgMLST interpretations were highly reproducible across sites, supporting the use of standardized core-genome typing for cross-country surveillance. The pilot demonstrates that heterogeneous WGS pipelines can still yield comparable, actionable typing data.

Survey of viruses associated with the whitefly Bemisia tabaci in cucurbits in Georgia, United States.

This study surveyed the virome of whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci) collected from cucurbit crops in Tifton, Georgia, over two consecutive years using RNA sequencing and bioinformatics analysis. The work characterizes viruses associated with this major agricultural pest, which causes over $100 million in annual vegetable losses through virus transmission, to better understand its vectoring potential and identify candidate viral biocontrol agents.

Assembly and comparative analysis of the mitochondrial genome of Pteroceltis tatarinowii Maxim. (Cannabaceae), a tertiary relict plant endemic to China.

vardictcpp: a C++ reimplementation of VarDict variant caller.

vardictcpp is a C++ reimplementation of the widely used VarDict variant caller, aiming to improve on the original Perl version's long run times and VarDictJava's high memory consumption. It provides a functionally equivalent tool that should enable faster and more memory-efficient variant calling, allowing more jobs to run in parallel on the same hardware.
